column1: # OWASP ZAP baseline rules for Kopi Kita.
# Every IGNORE line below has the same reason written in security/temuan-w2m4.md,
# and none of them is there "just to get the pipeline green".
# CSP still allows inline scripts and styles. The nonce-based CSP from the
# Next.js docs needs dynamic rendering for every page; Kopi Kita is statically
# rendered, so the documented nonce-free variant was used. Accepted risk with a
# written next step (tighten CSP when the app grows server-rendered pages).

column3: (CSP uses 'unsafe-inline' for script-src and style-src: nonce-based CSP requires dynamic rendering; recorded as an accepted risk with a next step)

column1: # Cross-origin isolation: COOP and CORP are now sent (PR fix/sec-cross-origin-headers).
# COEP require-corp stays off on purpose - it would block the PostHog assets
# from us-assets.i.posthog.com, which do not carry CORP headers.

column3: (COEP require-corp intentionally not sent: it would break PostHog assets; COOP and CORP are sent instead)

column1: # Informational findings, no action: ZAP recognises the framework, and the
# cache directives it reports come from Next.js asset handling.

column3: (Informational: ZAP identifies the site as a modern web application)
(Informational: cache directives come from Next.js asset handling, no secrets or personal data in them)

column1: # The only user-controlled value echoed into a page is ?category= on /menu; the
# client allow-lists the tabs and the API binds the value as a query parameter.

column3: (Informational: reflected parameter is the allow-listed ?category= on /menu, bound as a SQL parameter, no injection path)
